summary.text:
Hillingdon's Appendix G for 2026/27 heard at Cabinet on 19 February 2026 (Full Council 26 February), both passed. Compact 43-page bundle covering four statutory statements in one document — Capital Strategy (G1), Treasury Management Strategy (G2), Investment Strategy (G3) and Annual MRP Statement (G4). Report of Steve Muldoon, Corporate Director of Finance and S151 (verified from the cover budget report 65768 front sheet); co-author Matt Davis, Director Strategic & Operational Finance. Neither document publishes officer email addresses.

The paper opens by disclosing the Council is 'in the closing stages of agreeing Exceptional Financial Support with the government' totalling £173m over three years (£88m already in the 25/26 forecast, £62m requested for 26/27, £23m indicative for 27/28). EFS is delivered as a capitalisation directive treating revenue costs as capital, with MRP over 20 years. The cover report puts the annual servicing cost of MRP plus interest on cumulative EFS at £12.5m per annum by 28/29. Total CFR nearly doubles across the plan, from £587m (24/25 actual) to £1,139m by 30/31. Financing costs as a proportion of net revenue stream more than double from 6% (25/26) to 14% (28/29 onwards). The liability benchmark under the £25m minimum cash assumption falls from £20.8m at 25/26 to £3.6m by 30/31 — a very tight forecast trajectory close to minimum-risk borrowing.

On the current book: total secured loans £621.2m at 31 January 2026 (paragraph 90) — PWLB fixed £522.2m, temp LAs £61m, market/LOBOs £38m. Weighted rates: GF book 4.17%, HRA book 3.99%. Table 14 maturity profile has 23.04% of the fixed book in the under-12m bucket. Paragraph 81 reports that in August 2025 a £5m LOBO was called by the bank counterparty and repaid because the new offered rate was uneconomic against PWLB replacement — the same pattern already logged at Kent, Tameside, York, Wolverhampton, Harrow, Staffordshire and Bath & NE Somerset, and every LOBO call in our drafted set has been refused. The paper explicitly flags future call exercises as 'significant' likelihood and rules out new LOBO borrowing. Two notable service-loan positions: the £35m Hillingdon First facility (nothing drawn) and the £6m loan to the Burroughs Care Home SPV (THCC) at a fixed 8.19% — priced at 2.00% above the PWLB 40-year annuity rate at drawdown in August 2025.

Balance sheet identity ties cleanly at every reported year (25/26F: 793.2 − 736.9 − 10.0 = 46.3, exact match to the paper's own 'External Borrowing to meet CFR' line). The DSG deficit line footnote states it 'is not adjusted for LG Settlement changes announced on the 9th February 2026' — Cabinet was 10 days later; a refreshingly transparent flag on a moving target that peaks at £88.2m in 28/29 under the statutory override.

Loan-book reconciliation DOES NOT TIE. Our file at 31/1/26 holds 27 PWLB loans at £280.19m; the paper reports £522.2m PWLB — a £242m gap (46% of theirs). At 31/3/26 our file grows to 51 loans at £544.5m, well above the £116m of new borrowing the paper anticipated for the balance of the year, and still short of the implied year-end PWLB total. Most plausible explanation is our bc-loans Start-date coding (PIPELINE.md flags this exact trap). Reconciliation kept out of the email; recorded here.

The most consequential single line in the paper after the EFS itself sits in Appendix G4 page 41: 'In 2026/27 the Annuity Method will be applied to calculations of MRP charge for all debt.' No before/after impact quantified. Annuity back-loads MRP relative to equal-instalment methods and materially reshapes revenue charges across every year of the plan.

Email drafted around the LOBO call peer signal, the MRP method change, the liability benchmark shape and a specific compliment on the single-document format of Appendix G. Loan-book reconciliation deliberately omitted (fails). Draft machine-checked against the paper text; recipient line outstanding pending Steve Muldoon's email address. Send-by early September before the next monthly Cabinet treasury monitoring cycle.

officer.subject: Your August 2025 LOBO call, and one line in your Appendix G4
officer.body:
Hi Steve,

Apologies for the cold email. PWLBtoday is fairly new so you may not have come across us yet.

We're built for local authority treasury teams and nothing else: live PWLB rates at both daily fixings, a monthly breakdown of every loan the sector draws, every council's PWLB book priced daily against the DMO's repayment curve, and a training academy for officers and members. There's more — the predictor, the SONIA path, peer metrics, a daily brief — in the brochure at [BROCHURE URL]. We don't sell treasury products, and the data side is free and stays free.

To keep that data and our training relevant we built tools that watch committee papers across every council in the country, so we can see how a council's own figures compare with where the market has gone since. So below are a few thoughts on your Appendix G, ahead of the next monthly treasury monitoring cycle. You're not being singled out — every authority gets one of these — and there's no agenda in it. Bundling the Capital Strategy, Treasury Management Strategy, Investment Strategy and MRP statement into a single 43-page document, rather than splitting them across separate attachments where readers lose the thread, is a version of this report several of the councils we've read would benefit from copying.

Your paragraph 81 mentions the £5m LOBO called by the bank counterparty in August 2025 and repaid because the new rate offered was uneconomic against PWLB. That fits a pattern we have now seen repeatedly across the councils we've read this year — banks calling, councils declining the new rate, loans repaid at par. Every LOBO call in the drafts we have written up so far has been refused. With £38m of market/LOBO loans still on the book at 31 January 2026 (paragraph 90), and 4.53% of the maturity profile sitting in the LOBO 1st-call column at Table 14, the shape of the next call cycle is something the cross-council picture may be useful for.

One line worth flagging in Appendix G4, page 41: "In 2026/27 the Annuity Method will be applied to calculations of MRP charge for all debt." The paper doesn't quantify the before/after impact. Against a CFR going from £793m at the 25/26 forecast to £1,139m by 30/31 (Table 4), the switch to annuity reshapes the MRP profile across every year of the plan. The financing costs ratio in Table 11 already moves from 6% (25/26) to 14% (28/29 onwards); the MRP method choice is one of the levers inside that.

The liability benchmark in Table 12 falls to £3.6m by 30/31 on the £25m minimum cash assumption you use. That takes the forecast trajectory very close to the minimum-risk borrowing level, and any downside on reserves, working capital or the DSG line (which the table flags as not adjusted for the 9 February 2026 settlement changes) shifts the number. We build interactive liability benchmark pathways on live data — worth a look given where CIPFA is heading with the Prudential and Treasury Codes.

Every PWLB loan the sector holds is priced daily against the DMO's premature repayment curve at pwlbtoday.org/loan-analysis (indicative only; only the DMO can quote and we model no MRP or accounting treatment). The monthly sector picture is at pwlbtoday.org/pwlb-activity: July was £368m across 33 loans from 19 borrowers, average 5.02%.

Three of the training courses look most relevant to where the report sits. LOBOs and options, for the £38m and the August 2025 experience. MRP methods, given the annuity switch. And Debt rescheduling and premature repayment. There's also an Audit Committee Chair (Treasury) course written for members hearing this kind of report. All 115 courses are free to local authorities until the end of September at pwlbtoday.org/academy, and free accounts for the whole team.

And if you do find it useful, mentioning it to others would help us more than anything. We're small, word of mouth is most of our marketing, and every sign-up helps us prove the need.

Sign up free → https://pwlbtoday.org/
Follow on LinkedIn → https://www.linkedin.com/company/pwlbtoday/

Russell
https://www.linkedin.com/in/russelltew

Source: Appendix G — Capital, Treasury, Investment and MRP Strategies 2026/27, Cabinet, 19 February 2026.
